current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intel 4 process node production status and capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel 4, the first EUV lithography node, delivered significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7; it moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024 for the Intel Core Ultra processor and is expected to represent an increasing portion of production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their adoption of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for leading-edge process nodes in 2024, but differ in specific node nomenclature and manufacturing scope. Micron (MU) identifies its '1γ' node as the first to employ EUV lithography for DRAM volume shipments expected in 2025, having transitioned production in 2024 to 1α and 1β nodes. In contrast, Intel (INTC) identifies 'Intel 4' and 'Intel 3' as its first EUV lithography nodes, which moved to high-volume manufacturing in 2024 for processor production, specifically noting Intel 4 is expected to represent an increasing portion of production in 2025. While both leverage EUV for advanced nodes in the same timeframe, MU focuses on DRAM memory nodes (1γ) while INTC focuses on CPU logic nodes (Intel 4/3).

sentences.text: We expect volume shipments in 2025 of our next generation of DRAM, the 1γ (1-gamma) node, which will employ EUV lithography production.

▪Intel 4, our first EUV lithography node, delivers significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7. The Intel Core Ultra processor is our first high-volume client product on Intel 4 and began shipping to customers in 2023. Intel 4 moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024, and is expected to represent an increasing portion of our processor production and products in 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Process Node Manufacturing Status and Roadmap Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: As of the end of 2024, most products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while high-volume production of the Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes was shifted to Ireland. The company canceled the productization of Intel 20A to focus on the improved Intel 18A node, which is expected to enter high-volume production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures highlight the operational ramp-up of advanced process nodes in 2024, though they address different product categories. Micron states that the majority of its DRAM bit production in 2024 was on leading-edge 1α and 1β nodes. Similarly, Intel reports that as of the end of 2024, a significant majority of its products were manufactured using the Intel 7 node, while it successfully ramped its first EUV nodes (Intel 4 and Intel 3) to high-volume production in Ireland. Both companies illustrate a 2024 strategic shift toward higher-density, next-generation process technologies for their respective silicon products.

sentences.text: The majority of our DRAM bit production in 2024 was on leading-edge 1α (1-alpha) and 1ß nodes.

As of the end of 2024, a significant majority of our products were manufactured using our Intel 7 process node in Arizona and Israel, we successfully ramped our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes as our first EUV lithography nodes and shifted high-volume production of those nodes to Ireland, and we canceled the productization of our Intel 20A process node to focus efforts on the improved version of the node, Intel 18A, that we expect to put into high-volume production in 2025 with our new client family of products code-named Panther Lake.
